items.front: In Elastic Load Balancing, requests must go to different services by URL path. Which load balancer do you choose?
items.extra: Its listener rules can [forward requests based on the URL](../facts/elb.md#elb-alb-path-conditions-smaller-services).

items.front: In Elastic Load Balancing, partners must allow-list fixed IP addresses. Which load balancer do you choose?
items.back: A Network Load Balancer with Elastic IP addresses.
items.extra: You can [optionally associate one Elastic IP address](../facts/elb.md#elb-nlb-static-ip-per-az-optional-eip) with the network interface in each enabled zone.

items.front: In Elastic Load Balancing, all traffic must pass through third-party firewall appliances. Which load balancer do you choose?
items.extra: AWS names it for [deploying inline virtual appliances](../facts/elb.md#elb-gwlb-faq-when-inline-appliances).

items.front: In Elastic Load Balancing, does the load balancer replace an instance that fails its health checks?
items.back: No. It stops routing to it. EC2 Auto Scaling replaces it.
items.extra: With ELB health checks on the Auto Scaling group, [Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling replaces the unhealthy instance](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-elb-checks-reroute-and-replace).

items.front: In Elastic Load Balancing, the instances must decrypt TLS themselves. Which listener do you use?
items.back: A Network Load Balancer TCP listener on port 443.
items.extra: A TCP listener [passes encrypted traffic through to the targets](../facts/elb.md#elb-alb-https-decrypt-at-target-use-nlb-tcp).

items.front: In Elastic Load Balancing, cross-zone load balancing: on which load balancer types is it off by default?
items.extra: On these two types, [cross-zone load balancing is disabled by default](../facts/elb.md#elb-nlb-gwlb-cross-zone-off-by-default).

items.front: In Elastic Load Balancing, can you attach an Elastic IP address to an Application Load Balancer?
items.back: No. Only the Network Load Balancer has them.
items.extra: The AWS feature table marks [IP address - Static, Elastic](../facts/elb.md#elb-compare-static-elastic-ip-nlb-only) for the Network Load Balancer only.

items.front: In a Network Load Balancer created without security groups, can you add security groups later?
items.back: No. Only when you create it.
items.extra: Without security groups at creation, [you can't associate them](../facts/elb.md#elb-nlb-security-groups-only-at-creation) later.

items.front: In an Application Load Balancer, one HTTPS listener must serve three domains. What do you add?
items.back: Their certificates to the certificate list (SNI).
items.extra: A certificate list lets the listener [provide a different certificate for each domain](../facts/elb.md#elb-alb-sni-certificate-list-multiple-domains).

items.front: In an Application Load Balancer, every target fails its health checks. Does it stop sending requests?
items.back: No. It fails open and uses all targets.
items.extra: With only unhealthy targets, the load balancer [routes requests to all those targets](../facts/elb.md#elb-alb-fail-open-all-unhealthy).

items.front: In Elastic Load Balancing, targets must accept traffic only from the load balancer. What is the source of their rule?
items.extra: Set [the load balancer's security group as the source](../facts/elb.md#elb-target-sg-reference-lb-sg) in the ingress rule of the targets.

items.front: In Elastic Load Balancing, which load balancer can have a Lambda function as a target?
items.extra: Application Load Balancers are [the only load balancers that support](../facts/elb.md#elb-lambda-target-alb-only) the lambda target type.

items.front: In an Application Load Balancer, where does the target find the client's IP address?
items.extra: By default the load balancer [stores the IP address of the client](../facts/elb.md#elb-alb-xff-holds-client-ip) in that request header.

items.front: In an Application Load Balancer, duration-based or application-based stickiness: which one fits an application with its own session cookie?
items.extra: If the application has its own session cookie, use [application-based stickiness](../facts/elb.md#elb-alb-sticky-duration-vs-application-cookie).

items.front: In ACM, does ACM renew a certificate that you imported for your load balancer?
items.back: No. You renew imported certificates yourself.
items.extra: ACM [does not manage the renewal process](../facts/acm.md#acm-faq-imported-no-managed-renewal) for imported certificates.

items.front: In an Application Load Balancer, can a redirect action send HTTPS requests to HTTP?
items.back: No. HTTP to HTTPS works, not the reverse.
items.extra: In a redirect action, [You cannot redirect HTTPS to HTTP](../facts/elb.md#elb-alb-redirect-http-to-https).

items.front: In Elastic Load Balancing, internal or internet-facing: which load balancer's nodes have only private IP addresses?
items.extra: The nodes of an internal load balancer [have only private IP addresses](../facts/elb.md#elb-internal-nodes-private-ips-only).

items.front: In AWS PrivateLink, which load balancer types can sit behind a VPC endpoint service?
items.back: A Network or Gateway Load Balancer.
items.extra: Endpoint services require either a [Network Load Balancer or a Gateway Load Balancer](../facts/elb.md#elb-privatelink-needs-nlb-or-gwlb).

items.front: In Elastic Load Balancing, which feature moves a load balancer's traffic away from one impaired Availability Zone with a single action?
items.extra: Zonal shift moves traffic [away from an impaired Availability Zone](../facts/elb.md#elb-zonal-shift-what) to the healthy zones.

items.front: In Elastic Load Balancing, on which capacity dimension are you charged each hour?
items.back: Only the dimension with the highest usage.
items.extra: You are charged only on the [dimension with the highest usage](../facts/elb.md#elb-lcu-charged-on-highest-dimension).

items.front: In an Application Load Balancer, requests vary a lot in how long they take. Which routing algorithm fits?
items.extra: It sends requests to the targets with the [lowest number of in progress requests](../facts/elb.md#elb-alb-least-outstanding-requests-use).

items.front: In Elastic Load Balancing, which load balancer can you protect with an AWS WAF web ACL?
items.extra: With AWS WAF on an Application Load Balancer, rules can [block, allow, or monitor (count) web requests](../facts/elb.md#elb-waf-integrates-with-alb).

items.front: In an HTTPS listener, the certificate or the security policy: which one decides the TLS protocols and ciphers?
items.extra: A security policy is [a combination of protocols and ciphers](../facts/elb.md#elb-alb-security-policy-protocols-ciphers).

items.front: In Elastic Load Balancing, which load balancer can sign users in before requests reach the application?
items.extra: The AWS feature table marks [User Authentication](../facts/elb.md#elb-compare-user-authentication-alb-only) for the Application Load Balancer only.

items.front: In Elastic Load Balancing, the default deregistration delay is {{c1::300 seconds}}.
In an Application Load Balancer, the default connection idle timeout is {{c1::60 seconds}}.
In a Network Load Balancer, the default TCP idle timeout is {{c1::350 seconds}}.
In an Application Load Balancer, a target is unhealthy by default after {{c1::2 consecutive failed health checks}}.
In an Application Load Balancer, the default health check interval for instance and IP targets is {{c1::30 seconds}}.
In an Application Load Balancer, a duration-based stickiness cookie lasts {{c1::1 day}} by default.
In an Application Load Balancer, a Lambda function target gets a request body of at most {{c1::1 MB}}.
In a Gateway Load Balancer, traffic reaches the appliances with the {{c1::GENEVE protocol on port 6081}}.
